## What's new

- **BLAKE3 hashes.** On a KamPlexFS server which computes BLAKE3
  hashes, both the s3 remote with `provider = KamPlexFS` and the
  `kamplexfs` backend support them. `rclone hashsum blake3`,
  `rclone check` and `rclone sync --checksum` work with BLAKE3. Both
  backends work with servers which have MD5 turned off and only
  compute BLAKE3. Servers which don't compute BLAKE3 work as before
  with MD5 only.
- **Uploads are checked with BLAKE3.** Each upload is hashed as it is
  sent and fails if the server's BLAKE3 is different. With the s3
  remote, a multipart upload is followed by one HEAD request to read
  the hash, unless `no_head` is set explicitly. `--s3-disable-checksum`
  turns the check off for the s3 remote.
  `kamplexfs_blake3_concurrency` (s3) and `blake3_concurrency`
  (`kamplexfs`) limit how many uploads are hashed at once.
- **`hashes` option.** `hashes` in the remote's config chooses the
  hashes instead of using the ones the server lists. For example,
  `hashes = md5` turns BLAKE3 off, and `hashes = blake3` compares
  files by BLAKE3 only. A `kamplexfs` remote finds out the server's
  hashes from its bucket listing, which tokens restricted with
  `allowed_prefixes` can't make. Such remotes need `hashes` set to use
  BLAKE3.

Notes:

- The s3 remote's listings don't carry BLAKE3 hashes. The first file
  asked for in a directory is read with a HEAD request, and the rest
  of the directory with a bulk listing of its hashes.
- BLAKE3 hashes are never used to tell whether a file has changed, for
  example by the VFS cache of `rclone mount`.
- Files the server hasn't hashed yet, including files stored before
  the server computed BLAKE3, have an empty BLAKE3 hash. Transfers of
  those files are checked by size and modification time instead.
- A BLAKE3 hash from the server which isn't 64 lowercase hex digits
  is ignored, so the upload is not checked.

## Fixes

- An s3 remote with `provider = KamPlexFS` and no access key no longer
  crashes when it starts.
